edges.description: The lactate excess presents clinically as lactic acidosis.

Severe decompensation progressed to failure of several organs in the index patient.
Liver failure, with a prolonged prothrombin time, was part of the multiorgan failure.

After the acute brain injury, the index patient had paroxysmal episodes of sympathetic overactivity.
Protein catabolism during illness is proposed to increase H2S production beyond what the low residual SQOR activity can clear.

nodes.description: H2S comes from cysteine catabolism in host tissues and from gut bacteria. In the SqorDeltaN/DeltaN mouse, H2S levels rise and are lowered by metronidazole, implicating the gut microbial source. In patients the accumulation is thought to be intermittent: plasma sulfide was normal in a symptomatic patient between episodes and elevated in one asymptomatic sibling, which suggests that alternative routes can handle basal H2S load and that disease follows when supply exceeds them.

nodes.description: Biallelic SQOR variants leave very little SQOR protein and enzyme activity. The missense p.(Glu213Lys) disrupts hydrogen bonding and destabilizes the protein, and c.446delT is a frameshift. SQOR catalyses the first and committed step of mitochondrial sulfide oxidation, oxidizing H2S with coenzyme Q as electron acceptor and glutathione as sulfane sulfur acceptor, so its loss removes the main mitochondrial route for H2S disposal. Levels of the H2S-generating enzymes are unchanged.
